facts.claim: A quest starts or turns at Gang Ground.
The people of Gang Ground are caught in a quarrel the player can see.
A traveller can rest safely at Gang Ground.
Gang Ground tells part of the province's past.
Someone at Gang Ground has work for the player.
Gang Ground gives shelter for the night.
Something at Gang Ground records its past.
The families of a gang that works a channel live in the camp.
The camp is forty years old and is named for the ground the gang works.
The camp stands on a slope of firm ground between the Border road and the marsh.
The top terrace stays dry enough for a hatching shed.
The camp has a Hist a day upriver but no claim on it.
The families stay because the clutch is in the shed.
The hatching shed is kept warmer and cleaner than the sleeping sheds.
A nest of twig bundles and a carapace oven stand by the clutch.
Low shelters step down the slope on levelled terraces.
The hatching shed stands on the top terrace below the road.
The gang's barge lies at its pier below the camp, a Bretic hull with a shed on the deck and a crane at the bow.
A timber stack, a chopping block, a hand cart and sacks stand about the camp.
Cut planks and tools lie on the barge deck.
The way in descends from the Border road to the hatching shed door.
The yard way runs down the terraces from the hatching shed.
A way down leads to the landing and the barge pier.
A second way out climbs the two Hist roots on the west bank.
The families will not move away from the egg clutch.
The families have put together provisions for a stranger.
The shelters are bamboo, reed thatch, and hide over poles.
The ground is packed earth and the barge is old ship timber.
The mood is domestic; the ledger is a walk away.
The camp is mud and thatch.
The hatching shed's lamp burns warm amber at night.
The camp smells of cooking and wet reed.
A low continuous sound comes from the hatching shed.
The families are people whose kin are on the roll, keeping a life going within walking distance of it.
If the clutch is lost, the families go somewhere the ledger cannot follow.
